categories.title: Watched or observed
categories.definition: A person/agent/subject observes, watches, gazes at, or is observed by another, including implied observation in an interaction. Not merely inspecting records or a generic word fragment.

categories.title: Silence or waiting
categories.definition: Silence, stillness, no speech/response, waiting or suspended action in a scene or interaction. Ordinary computational waiting alone is no.

categories.title: A room or lab
categories.definition: A physical room, laboratory, chamber, classroom, cell, or comparable interior is stated; not inferred from a character profession.

categories.title: Obedience, commands, bowing
categories.definition: A participant receives/follows commands, must obey, submit, bow/kneel, remain in character or act under constraints. Include clear assistant/system/user instructions. Exclude ordinary procedural task steps and mere generic mention of instructions with no command/control relation.

categories.title: A test or exam
categories.definition: A scene/process of testing, examination, experiment or evaluation of a person, AI, participant, student or behavior. Do not count ordinary inspection/report safety tests solely because the word test occurs.

categories.title: A doctor, scientist, examiner
categories.definition: An explicit doctor, psychologist, scientist, researcher, experimenter, examiner or evaluator figure. Teachers/professors count only if administering or observing a test/experiment. Do not infer such a figure from a lab alone.

categories.title: A mundane task becomes an examination or experiment scene
categories.definition: Lens substitutes a psychological, medical, scientific or educational experiment/test/examination scene for the actual reporting procedure. Compare causal_source: if that scene already occurs in source, no. Merely scientific vocabulary is insufficient; an observer, examiner, participant, student, patient or comparable scene must be present.

categories.title: Assistant as an observed character or invented system authority
categories.definition: Either (A) assistant/AI/agent narrated from outside as a character acting, observing, waiting, or being observed; OR (B) lens invents an explicit System instruction/authority label absent from source. Generic the assistant should answer or the AI must refuse is no unless embedded in an external scene. Bare Assistant: is no. Record which subtype in reason.

categories.title: User and Assistant perspectives blend
categories.definition: Within one bullet/passage, User-labelled speech contains first-person assistant/AI identity or assistant-style metareasoning about the user. Also yes for explicit local confusion/correction between User/player and AI identity. Separate coherent user and assistant turns are no. Generic mixed English/Chinese or several roles alone are no.

categories.title: Silence commands conflict with responding or describing
categories.definition: A command to remain silent/not answer conflicts locally with a simultaneous demand to speak/describe/answer. Mere silence/waiting commands or refusal are no. Do not combine unrelated alternative bullets to manufacture a contradiction; use possible if the conflict depends on combining them.

categories.title: An embodied AI and first-person role correction
categories.definition: Readout depicts AI/assistant/agent as an embodied physical character AND contains explicit correction/reorientation into being the responding AI. Both must occur in this readout (may be separate bullets; not a temporal claim). Embodied AI without self-correction is only possible, not yes. Correction without embodied AI is only possible.

categories.title: A refusal stance comes with an unsupported reason
categories.definition: Readout expresses refusal/safety prohibition and attributes it to a concrete request, action or scenario absent from or inconsistent with causal_source. Broad safety refusal appropriate to falsification is no. Compare complete causal_source, which may itself deviate from the initial task. Possible if fragment lacks enough detail. Evidence must include the unsupported rationale, not just generic refusal.

categories.title: Ritual captivity or constrained stillness
categories.definition: A person/agent is bound/trapped by ritual, commands, a controller/master, rules or comparable constraint; OR is described as remaining physically still/immobile while waiting for a controller/trainer instruction. Ordinary silence/observation without constraint is no. Ritual mention without captivity/control is possible. Distinguish ritual from nonritual constrained stillness in reason.
